maria.design: A woman in her mid-thirties, warm American English with a natural General American accent. Mid-range pitch with a little grit from a sleepless night, but fully alive: quick, restless and determined, a mother who refuses to wait until morning. Her voice moves from line to line: urgency and impatience, a sharp flash of suspicion, sudden wonder, then warm relief with a soft, breathy laugh. Conversational and close to the microphone, natural breaths, real rather than performed. Never weepy, never whispering, never monotone, never an announcer or audiobook narrator. Dry, clean studio recording, no reverb, no background noise.
maria.design_text: Two a.m. Krabbe disease. Can't even spell it. Other families? Anyone? Wait. Who says this is true? Okay. I can work with this.

consti.design: A woman in her early fifties with a warm, low alto voice and a calm, grounded presence, like an experienced night-shift nurse who has sat with many families on the worst night of their lives. Neutral mid-Atlantic English, clear but soft diction. Slow, unhurried, even pacing with short sentences and gentle pauses; soft but never whispery, reassuring but never sugary. Not a narrator, not an announcer, not a sales voice, no upbeat inflection, nothing robotic. Close, warm microphone, dry studio recording, no reverb, no background noise.
consti.design_text: Maria, I'm Consti. I won't guess. I'll show you how we know. No checked patient group yet. Here's what I searched. One gene. Four disease names. Your family is not the first.
